# Deviload 2.12.0

**Devil Music in liquid glass.** The player, its panels and its windows move smoothly, and the lyrics now follow you everywhere.

- The play button is a glass orb in your theme's colours that breathes with the bass: violet in Aurora, iridescent in Prism, amber in Vinyl, and clear glass tinted by the cover in Ambient, Light and Noir. The timeline fills like a glass tube with bubbles drifting through it, the volume is the same tube, and the mini-player gets all of it too.
- Panels, windows and menus glide open and shut. A new song flows into the player bar, the player's colour follows the new cover, and an album opened from a card takes its cover with it into the page.
- One Lyrics button shows the words wherever the player is. In the full player the lines move in and out of focus, the music video can show them like subtitles, a floating strip keeps them on your desktop, and Share a line makes a picture of up to four lines to copy or save.
- Your listening week, month and year open in a stats window with your top artists and songs.

### Devil Music

Songs answer the pointer. Rows catch a soft light and a click ripples across them, cards tilt towards the pointer with a glow of their own cover, and covers show a glass play button. The heart fills with red when you like a song, the speaker shows as many waves as the volume is loud, and the song menu opens as liquid glass. Reordering the queue lifts the song under the pointer and shows where it will land.

Search results arrive as a wave, and the original song comes before live takes, covers and remixes you did not ask for. When the top result is a music video, the album recording of the same song leads instead, so its lyrics stay in time; the video is still one click away. Earlier results stay while you type, and the arrow keys move through them. Wide video pictures fill square covers instead of sitting between black bars.

Hovering the timeline shows the time and the line sung there, and a click on the song length switches to the time left. The mouse wheel seeks over the timeline and changes the volume over the speaker. Album and artist headers sink back and blur as the page scrolls.

The phone remote and Listen together are redesigned, and the remote shows a sharp cover and the current line. Pausing when another app plays sound and levelling the loudness between songs are new options in playback settings, both off by default.

Choose Only Devil Music on the first start or later in music settings to open straight into music; updates and your library stay the same. A short glass tour introduces the player on the first start.

Scrolling stays smooth while music plays, searches, Home and the side panels no longer stall, and the window moves and resizes without the interface lagging behind. Lyrics stay in step with what you hear.

### Deviload

The download queue is checked less often while nothing is downloading, and the Deviload tour uses the same glass style.

On Windows, run the setup EXE over your installed copy to keep your library and settings. Deleting your playlists and app data is only an option in the uninstaller and is off by default.
